scenario: Felix has sent retailer Quillmart an identical, complete data access request every single business day for the past three weeks, each demanding a fresh full copy of all his data; Quillmart has fully answered the first one and confirms nothing in his data has changed since. Quillmart refused to act on the latest in the series.
policy: Generally, a controller must respond to a data subject access request by providing a copy of the personal data within one month. However, where requests from a data subject are manifestly unfounded or excessive, in particular because of their repetitive character, the controller may refuse to act on the request.
question: Was Quillmart permitted to refuse the latest request?
